body.statement: For one normalized conjunction, the single-conjunction representative transition is sound and complete: within any block, all values outside the distinct intervention constants induce the same refinement and future support, so one fresh value suffices. Across all branching blocks the number of representative column choices is at most \(3^{(h-1)/3}\). For \(r\) normalized conjunctions, the joint-score representative transition is sound and complete after truth flags are included, and the number of representative column choices is at most \( (r+1)^{h-1}\).
body.justification: The representative bounds convert normalized-state sufficiency into alphabet-independent transition complexity.
body.gap: Published response-signature and finite-model algorithms enumerate alphabet-indexed function values rather than quotienting untested constants within each normalized prefix block.
body.consumer: Implementers obtain a complete branching rule that scans large alphabets only polynomially.
body.proof_tex:
First consider one normalized conjunction and a block \(T\in\pi_i\) at coordinate \(q=i+1\).  All natural worlds in \(T\) call the same row by \texttt{thm:partition-continuation}.  If there is no natural world, the column on \(T\) is fixed by interventions.  If natural pins disagree, no output can meet them.  If they agree on a value, there is one possible natural output.  In the remaining case let \(C_T\) be the set of distinct intervention constants in \(T\).  For \(z,z'\in\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T\), the natural worlds form one new subblock, separate from every intervention-constant subblock, under either choice.  Thus \(z\) and \(z'\) give the same refinement and violate no natural pin.  The exact-continuation theorem gives the same future support.  A choice \(z\in C_T\), by contrast, merges the natural subblock with the worlds carrying that particular constant and is therefore retained separately.  This proves soundness and completeness of \(\mathsf C_1\)'s representative list, including the case \(\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T=\varnothing\).

For the count, let a branching block have \(a\) intervened and \(b\geq1\) natural worlds, and put \(t=a+b\).  It has at most \(a+1\leq t\) representatives.  For integers \(t=1,2,3\), direct calculation gives \(t\leq3^{t/3}\).  For \(t\geq3\), the derivative of \(x\mapsto \log(x)/x\) is \((1-\log x)/x^2<0\), whence
\[
 \frac{\log t}{t}\leq\frac{\log3}{3},
 \qquad t\leq3^{t/3}.
\]
The block containing the factual world is nonbranching because that natural output is pinned by \(v\).  If \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\) are the sizes of all branching blocks, then \(\sum_jt_j\leq h-1\), and therefore
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^m t_j
 \leq3^{\sum_jt_j/3}
 \leq3^{(h-1)/3}.
\]

For the joint compiler, attach a flag vector \(a_i\in\{0,1\}^r\) to the partition.  Before branching at coordinate \(q\), coalesce repeated identical tests.  If a live term tests two distinct constants at the same world-coordinate, that term necessarily fails at this coordinate, so set its flag to zero before forming representatives.  This is a value-preserving Boolean simplification, including the contradictory/repeated-term case; afterward each live term tests at most one constant per world at coordinate \(q\).

For an unpinned natural group in \(T\), let \(C_T\) now contain the distinct intervention constants and the constants tested on natural worlds by live terms.  Two outputs outside \(C_T\) have the same equality relation to every intervention constant and fail exactly the same current tests.  They consequently give the same refined partition and the same updated flag vector; \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} then gives the same future support.  Retaining every member of \(C_T\cap\mathcal D_q\) and one member of \(\mathcal D_q\setminus C_T\), when nonempty, is therefore both sound and complete.

If \(T\) contains \(a\) intervened and \(b\geq1\) natural worlds, there are at most \(a+rb+1\) representatives.  Since \(r\geq1\) and \(t=a+b\),
\[
 a+rb+1\leq rt+1\leq(r+1)^t,
\]
where the last inequality follows by retaining the first two terms in the binomial expansion of \((1+r)^t\).  Again the factual block is nonbranching, so multiplication over branching blocks gives
\[
 \prod_T(r+1)^{|T|}
 \leq(r+1)^{h-1}.
\]
The update rule is conjunction with precisely the tests at the new coordinate, so a dead flag needs no further information and a live flag records exactly that all processed tests passed.  Thus equality of the partition and flags is a right congruence for future transitions.  This proves the claimed joint soundness, completeness, and transition bound.
